intended_application: Draft narrative sections of externally published financial reports from approved figures.
organization: Hypothetical regional bank with formal reporting controls
business_need: Explore whether drafting support can reduce repetitive work without weakening review or traceability.
users_stakeholders: Finance analysts, reporting owners, compliance reviewers and external readers
adoption_posture: Conservative / risk averse; no automatic publication
capabilities_constraints: Controlled reporting systems and expert reviewers; confidential inputs; no approved model deployment or validated report-generation workflow supplied
risk_consequence_context: Incorrect or unsupported statements could mislead external readers. Published errors are harder to reverse; auditability and approval are essential case requirements.
management_question: Does the creation history justify reliance on AI-authored external reporting, or only a bounded internal investigation?
time_horizon: A proposed four-week feasibility review; external release is outside the test
additional_context:
This is a constructed teaching case, not a claim about an actual company. Evidence packet follows. Treat source summaries as bounded verified notes; verify new claims independently.

[S1] Bengio et al. (2003-02). A Neural Probabilistic Language Model. https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v3/bengio03a.html
Checked 2026-10-04, Abstract. Evidence: Learning word representations and word-sequence probabilities jointly helped neural language models generalize beyond observed sequences. Limitation: An early predecessor, not the sole origin of generative AI.

[S2] Vaswani et al. (2017-06-12). Attention Is All You Need. https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762
Checked 2026-10-04, Abstract. Evidence: The Transformer replaced recurrent sequence processing with attention and demonstrated more parallelizable training on translation tasks. Limitation: Translation experiments do not establish business-report accuracy.

[S3] Brown et al. (2020-05-28). Language Models are Few-Shot Learners. https://arxiv.org/html/2005.14165v4
Checked 2026-10-04, Abstract and sections 2.2 and 2.3. Evidence: GPT-3 combined scaled autoregressive modeling, large curated text mixtures and GPU-cluster training, and demonstrated few-shot task performance with limitations. Limitation: Historical benchmarks do not measure this organization or a current vendor model.

[S4] Ouyang et al. (2022-03-04). Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback. https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155
Checked 2026-10-04, Abstract. Evidence: Supervised demonstrations and human preference feedback improved instruction following; the resulting models still made mistakes. Limitation: Better alignment with user intent is not a factual-accuracy guarantee.
